  - Writes: unique `mkstemp` temp files; the version is rechecked under a lock before every swap, including the OneDrive retry; `create`/`init` never overwrite (Windows `os.rename`, POSIX `os.link`).
  - Paths: scan and write paths are checked to stay inside the project folder.
  - Links: `link` on a single-value role refuses to replace an existing link (CONFLICT); a generated link must resolve to its target; `unlink` works on broken links.
  - List values: items containing quotes or brackets are quoted, and quotes only open a token.
  - Create: names containing `[ ] | # ^ / \` are refused; fields cannot override id/type/canonical_name; ids are deduplicated with `-2` etc.; the body is passed through untouched.
  - Merge: empty-list expectations merge correctly, and body conflicts return the current body.
  - Errors: ValueError/OSError become LoreError INVALID/IO_ERROR at the ops boundary, and newlines in values are refused.
  - Written keys match `[a-z_]+` (spec FR-2a added).
  - MCP: the envelope is validated (`jsonrpc` "2.0", string/int id, method); modern requests need `clientCapabilities`; output is ASCII-escaped, so lone surrogates can't crash the server.
- Note: Codex's sandbox blocks temp-file writes in read-only mode, so its in-review test run is not meaningful. Claude runs the suite.
- **Feature 001 done:** 76 tests green.

### Feature 010 specified: progressive story wiki (2026-10-18 to 2026-10-19)
- Owner shaped the request in conversation:
  - It is a progressive wiki with an index per type that lists only what the reader has met by chapter X.
  - Clicking an entry opens a progressive card with its own chapter toggle. Character cards show the critical things (beliefs, what they know, where they are, relationships).
  - Factions, locations, important items and vehicles get the same cards, and so do kinds of things ("standard alien battle tank").
  - Someone seen before being named is listed under the reader's description until named.
  - A secret identity is a separate card until the reveal chapter.
  - A complete mode shows everything, with one card holding all of a character's identities.
- Owner: the build also applies the feature to the three sagas. The saga systems must keep working exactly as they do, with the progressive wiki added on top.
- Decision: in the sagas, stamped facts live in a separate `Story Wiki/` folder of companion pages, never in the Wiki pages. Reason: `profiles.assemble` puts each participant's whole Wiki page into the drafting packet (60 KB cap, fails above it), so facts that are no longer true would mislead drafting and could overflow the packet. Hand-written worlds keep stamps in their own pages. Undo: point `story_wiki` at nothing and stamp the pages instead.
- Decision: the chapter picker filters only the Wiki tab, and progressive cards hide frontmatter fields, because dates give deaths away. Per-field stamps are on the Later list. This revises the first answer given to the owner ("one picker filters every view").
- Decision: AI writes facts only through the new `fact-add`/`fact-end` operations (CLI, MCP, editor), never by hand-editing stamps. Each saga gets a project `.mcp.json` running the vendored `lore mcp`. Scripted steps use the CLI with `--json`.
- Decision: the saga update runs after `freeze N`, as a new shared skill plus one pointer. No stage, gate or existing instruction changes. If it is skipped, the Story Wiki is behind and nothing breaks.
- Spec written: specs/010-progressive-wiki/spec.md, on branch `feat/010-progressive-wiki` from `main` d0b564a. HANDOFF and KICKOFF-PROMPT rewritten for run 4. Nothing built yet.
- Owner requested a third wiki, the planning wiki: the intended end state, feeding the cards, then the draft, then the full and progressive wikis. Edits trigger an AI review of everything linked to the change. Recorded in BUILD-PLAN under "Planning wiki".
- Owner decisions (2026-10-19): the World Bible stays the master; conflicts with written chapters are flagged to the author, never applied; build 010 first, then specify the planning wiki as feature 011. Run 4's kickoff prompt keeps 011 out of scope.
- Owner: the planning wiki draws on every planning document (military bible, character sheets, dialogue documents and the rest), and its pages are well linked: kind pages list notable members, character cards list their saved dialogues, and an "Appears in" section comes from the chapter cards. Proposal recorded in BUILD-PLAN: Lorekeeper computes every link list mechanically (tags, Conversations headings and speakers, whole-word name and alias search over the parsed cards), so the AI never reads the cards for them.
- Owner decision: undecided material (plot ideas, opportunities, unapproved decisions) appears in the planning wiki, clearly labelled as ideas and kept apart from decided facts.
